newsitem.title: UK: No decision made on BAe Indonesia deal-UK.
newsitem.headline: No decision made on BAe Indonesia deal-UK.

text.p: No decision has yet been taken on whether the export licence allowing British Aerospace to sell 16 Hawk fighters to Indonesia should be revoked, a Foreign Office spokesman said on Friday.
The Financial Times reported that the 160 million stg deal would go ahead despite allegations that Indonesia was using jets it had acquired earlier against opponents in East Timor.
Junior Trade Minister Barbara Roche said in a parliamentary answer earlier this week that the government was seeking legal advice on the lawfulness of the possible revocation of export licences.
The spokesman said a decision on the Indonesian deal would be taken in the light of that advice.

Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said on Thursday Britain was reviewing the criteria for its arms exports, and stressed the new Labour government's commitment to put human rights at the heart of its foreign policy.
The spokesman said that future arms deals would be judged in the light of the outcome of the review, which it was hoped to complete before parliament begins its summer recess on July 31.
